pg_advisory_xact_lock is acquired after pool.begin() checks out a connection, so a burst of concurrent same-conversation spawns each hold a pooled connection while blocked on the lock; a hashtextextended collision would also serialize unrelated conversations. Bounded in practice by low spawn frequency + the cap this guard enforces.
resolution: Inherent to a per-conversation serialization lock over a pooled connection; bounded by the cap + spawn is not a hot path. Documented in a code comment. Not promotable (low, single-angle, not security/data-loss/authz).

finding: INV-3 reachable-violated: the completed/failed dedup clause keys off created_at (spawn time). A run longer than SPAWN_DEDUP_WINDOW_SECS (300s) already has created_at OUTSIDE the window when it completes and re-injects, so the immediate identical re-spawn is NOT deduped; because runs are sequential the concurrency CAP never fires either — a sustained loop for any task >5min, exactly what the feature must break. Fix: key the terminal clause off updated_at (mark_status stamps updated_at=NOW() on the terminal transition = completion time).

The INV-3 acceptance test seeds the recently-completed run at created_at=now and the negative control at created_at=1h-ago, but never exercises a run COMPLETED recently yet CREATED before the window (a >300s task) — the actual reachable INV-3 violation — so it passes with the created_at/updated_at bug present.
